population.definition: Census population (census date 2024-05-20) of the city 'Djibouti (Djibouti-Ville)' as a sum of three communes (Balbala, Boulaos, Ras Dika); no formal boundary definition given on the page. Figures marked final.

source.title: Djibouti: Administrative Division (Djibouti-Ville)
source.publisher: citypopulation.de (data from INSTAD, Institut National de la Statistique de Djibouti)
source.quote: 767,250 Population [2024] – census

facts.claim: France established a base at Obock on the north shore of the Gulf of Tadjoura in 1862, bought from the sultan of Tadjoura; the administrative centre was later moved to Djibouti.

source.title: Djibouti - La période coloniale
source.author: Colette Dubois, Alain Gascon, Jean-Louis Miège
source.quote: ayant transféré le centre administratif de leur possession à Djibouti

facts.claim: The year 1888 marked the decline of Obock and the birth of Djibouti as a bridgehead between north-east Africa and Arabia.

source.title: Le commerce des armes à Djibouti de 1888 à 1914
source.publisher: Revue française d'histoire d'outre-mer (Outre-Mers), tome 58, n°213, pp. 407-432 (via Persée)
source.author: Agnès Picquart
source.quote: marqua le déclin irrémédiable d'Obock et la naissance de Djibouti comme tête de pont

facts.claim: Site choice: Governor Lagarde judged the Obock roadstead too narrow and unsafe and chose Ras Djibouti for its large sheltered roadstead and access to the Ethiopian plateaus; the government moved there in 1892.

source.title: Le port de commerce de Djibouti
source.publisher: Revue historique des Armées, 21st year, no. 1 (via Persée)
source.author: P. Douteau
source.quote: trop étroite et peu sûre

facts.claim: Djibouti became capital of the Côte française des Somalis in 1896 (Lagarde moved the seat there in 1894, per Universalis); the town grew with the railway to Addis Ababa built 1897-1917. Note: Douteau gives 1892 for the move, Universalis 1894; sources differ.

source.title: Djibouti, ville
source.author: Alain Gascon
source.quote: qui devint, en 1896, la capitale de la Côte française des Somalis.

facts.claim: The territory was renamed Territoire français des Afars et des Issas in July 1967; independence was set for 27 June 1977 after a May 1977 referendum.

source.title: Djibouti - Vers l'indépendance (1967-1977)
source.author: Colette Dubois, Alain Gascon, Jean-Louis Miège
source.quote: la date du 27 juin 1977 pour l'accession à l'indépendance du nouvel État

facts.claim: The port developed first as a coaling station and then as a railhead for trains from Ethiopia; the city handles most of East Africa's trade through its seaport (EBSCO).

source.title: How Djibouti uses its stability and location to its advantage
source.publisher: Oxford Business Group, The Report: Djibouti 2023
source.quote: first as a coaling station and then as a railhead for trains coming from Ethiopia

places.name: Marché Central (Central Market)
places.what: Djibouti City's central market, listed with the Hamoudi Mosque and the seaport as the city's main features. EBSCO notes that most visitors to Djibouti see the central market and Hamoudi Mosque.

facts.label: Listed feature of the city
facts.value: The city has a central market, called marché central.

source.title: Djibouti
source.author: Richard Means
source.quote: Djibouti City features a marché central ("central market")

photo.author: Marc Baronnet (description: 'Market, centre of Djibouti'; not verified to show the Marché Central itself; year 2000)

places.name: Hamoudi Mosque
places.what: A mosque in central Djibouti City that EBSCO calls the nation's largest. A heritage listing gives its construction as 1906 by Haji Hamoudi.

facts.label: Size
facts.value: Largest mosque in the country (per EBSCO).

source.title: Djibouti
source.author: Richard Means
source.quote: the nation's largest Islamic mosque (Hamoudi Mosque)

facts.label: Built
facts.value: 1906 by Haji Hamoudi (single source, specialist site, tier uncertain; treat as unconfirmed)

source.title: Hamoudi Mosque (Mosquée Al-Hamoudi)
source.quote: The mosque was built in 1906 by Haji Hamoudi.

photo.author: Tyke (alt: File:Minaret of Hamoudi Mosque overlooking Djibouti City's central bus terminal (May 2024).jpg, CC BY-SA 4.0, Ch1pabeck)

places.name: Port of Djibouti
places.what: The seaport of Djibouti City, the reason the town was founded. It serves as the main trade outlet for landlocked Ethiopia; the container terminal is at Doraleh outside the city.

facts.label: Origin
facts.value: Developed as a coaling station, then a railhead for Ethiopia.

source.title: How Djibouti uses its stability and location to its advantage
source.quote: first as a coaling station and then as a railhead for trains coming from Ethiopia

facts.label: Role today
facts.value: A major trans-shipment point for goods to and from Ethiopia.

source.title: Djibouti: Country profile
source.quote: a major trans-shipment point for goods entering or leaving Ethiopia

facts.label: Doraleh
facts.value: A new regional port at Doraleh handles oil and containers.

source.author: Alain Gascon
source.quote: le nouveau port d'éclatement régional de Doraleh (pétrole et conteneurs)
